articles.summary: The best bath towel we have reviewed this past year, by Parachute, is 20% off from now through Cyber Monday. So is our favorite filtered showerhead. Welcome to Worth it, where Filter editors spotlight one genuinely good discount on something we have tested and loved.
body: This week, we are spotlighting a discount on our top bath towel.

Parachute’s Organic Plush Bath Towel is our favorite bath towel, and has maintained its crown through several rounds of towel testing this past year at the Filter US. Its durability, strong water absorbency and quality Turkish cotton material continue to impress Jon Chan, our head towel reviewer. He likened the Parachute to a “luxury bathrobe”. Its performance impressed the whole Filter US team so much that it earned a spot as one of the 10 best home gift ideas in our 2026 Filter holiday gift guide.

“I think this towel offers good bang for your buck,” wrote Chan. “There are towel brands like Frette that sell towels for more than $200 a pop and major retailers where they cost under $10. The Organic Super Plush sits at the perfect crossroads of value and cost.”
Right now, our best bath towel is 20% off during Parachute’s sitewide Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale. This is the lowest price we have seen on it since 20 May, when it was a few dollars cheaper.

articles.title: Sleep paralysis: when you’re awake, but can’t move – or even breathe | Letters
articles.summary: Readers recount their terrifying experiences of sleep paralysis in response to an article by Amy Fleming. I experienced sleep paralysis and hypnagogic hallucinations from childhood and into adulthood, with the episodes only waning in my 30s ( Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep…
body: I experienced hallucinations in the form of severe perspective distortion (oversized bed and rooms) and full hallucinations/dream states, auditory hallucinations (screaming and loud thumping) and, of course, paralysis. I didn’t know at what point I was asleep or if I had woken and could easily slip back into a hypnagogic state. I only became aware of this state as an adult, having been referred to a psychiatrist on an unrelated matter.

Some of the episodes were literally the stuff of nightmares. I have always had exceptionally vivid dreams and rarely do I go through a night without a dream waking me up (or so it seems). Once I understood what was happening, it was less terrifying and more fascinating, though the actual physical state cannot fail to be frightening.

Sleep paralysis struck me years before I learned, at an exhibition at the Wellcome Institute, that this was not just me being weird in my sleep, but a proper thing with a name. And yes, it is absolutely petrifying. I still remember how relieved I was on the one hand and fascinated on the other by all the evidence of sleep paralysis through the centuries at this exhibition.

articles.title: Have yourself a stress-free Christmas | Letters
articles.summary: Tara Padfield will be buying her marmalade and leaving the trees in the woods; Jen Arnall-Culliford says cooking in advance is key. Plus a letter from Alan Ravenscroft. I read Ammar Kalia’s article ( Christmas is all in the preparation!
body: Apparently, the secret to a stress-free Christmas involves roasting a kilogram of chicken wings and simmering stock for hours, making marmalade from scratch, infusing gin with Sichuan peppercorns and, should we have a spare afternoon, heading into the woods to forage for Douglas fir needles. I had naively imagined that time-saving tips might actually save time.
Instead, we are encouraged to embark on an elaborate programme of culinary projects, requiring specialist ingredients, considerable effort and a seemingly inexhaustible supply of enthusiasm.

Every year we have a Christmas dinner that is cooked in advance and frozen. In our house that is usually chilli con carne, but we have done curries and other dishes. The main aim is to be able to do the bulk of the cooking on a weekend in late November or early December.

Many in this session agreed the most successful family trips provide opportunities for separating and coming back together. Three itinerary choices in one day are ideal, so younger folks can be out and about, with the whole family reuniting for mealtimes and perhaps an afternoon activity. articles.title: Behind the Scenes of the Inaugural Bon Appétit LIVE
articles.summary: Top chefs, Test Kitchen editors, and passionate home cooks gathered for an unforgettable day of hands-on pie and lobster classes, tastings, and panels.
body: This past weekend the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen in New York City opened its doors to the public for Bon Appétit Live, an immersive day of cooking demos and classes, talks with chefs and recipe experts, Test Kitchen tours, games, prizes, and plenty to eat and drink.

The day kicked off with a warm welcome from Bon Appétit’s editor-in-chief Jamila Robinson, who exclaimed that “the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen is the heart of our brand.” Robinson also shared that Bon Appétit just launched a new cooking app containing tens of thousands of recipes from the Test Kitchen archives.
Guests fueled up with an impressive array of curated breakfast treats alongside refreshing beverages from S.Pellegrino, before moving on to interactive experiences.

Each guest left ready for holiday baking season with new pie-making skills, and a ceramic pie dish from East Fork’s new bakeware collection, featuring clay and glaze made in-house with materials sourced in the Southeast. Before moving on to their next experience, Mastrianni encouraged everyone to keep honing their skills, emphasizing, “Practice makes pie. Progress, not perfection.”

articles.title: Office Hours: Saie’s Laney Crowell on the Beauty of Doing Good
articles.summary: For the Saie founder, feeling good and doing good go hand in hand. Here, she shares the rituals, routines, and philosophies that guide her days.
body: For Laney Crowell, “feel good, do good” is not just the core philosophy of her beauty brand, Saie, but how she lives her life. “So much of beauty is not only who you are on the inside, but the actions that you take,” she says, emphasizing “the importance of taking action, especially in things that you are excited and passionate about.”

The driving force behind Saie was Crowell’s growing desire to make beauty better by creating formulas that are not just safe for your skin but also good for it. She wanted to create products that spoke to her as a self-professed “expert consumer.” “I’ve always struggled with really sensitive, acne-prone skin,” she says. “I had an aha moment where I realized that my makeup was what was making me break out. I started a blog [called The Moment ] to have the conversation. It was niche, but at the same time, I was one of the only people having this conversation.” Saie was born from this community building seven years ago.
